title: Canaries and honeytokens: would you know an intruder is already inside?
short: Plant five decoys on the paths intruders take, route every trip to someone on call and test each one quarterly.
answer: This month, plant decoys on the paths intruders take first, such as a Kerberoastable honeytoken account, a fake password file on a share and fake cloud keys on admin and developer machines, and route every trip to whoever handles high-severity alerts at night. Treat each trip as an intrusion until you can name the person or tool that caused it.
audience: IT and security teams in small and mid-size organizations, especially on Active Directory, Microsoft 365 and AWS

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Put decoys where intruders already look.
items.text: Attackers crack service tickets for accounts with a service principal name (SPN) offline, as FIN7 and Wizard Spider have[^attkerb], and search shares for stored passwords[^attfiles]. A honeytoken account with an SPN and a fake password file catch both.

items.title: Send every trip to someone who acts at night.
items.text: Route them like the logging sheet's critical alerts, to a named owner and deputy. Ask your MDR provider in writing whether it acts on them: Microsoft's Defender Experts covers only High and Medium incidents, not custom detections[^dexfaq].

items.title: Build on tools you already run.
items.text: Defender for Identity, Windows auditing, CloudTrail and Microsoft 365 alert policies keep alert data in systems you control. In a controlled test with over 130 red teamers, everyone facing decoys tripped one before exploiting a real machine[^tularosa].

items.title: Trip each canary yourself.
items.text: Test it when placed and every quarter, timing the alert until a person answers. Microsoft 365 alert policies take up to 24 hours to start[^alertpol]; Thinkst's canary AWS keys can take 2 to 30 minutes[^ctaws].

items.title: Keep a register and tell almost no one.
items.text: Record each decoy's location, trigger and alert path for the few admins who need it, so nobody uses one by mistake. In the NCSC's trials, 90% of participants said they wouldn't announce using deception[^ncsctrial].

items.title: A honeytoken account in Active Directory.
items.text: Create an unused user with an attractive name, an SPN, a long random password and no rights. Tag it **Honeytoken** in Defender for Identity (Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Security, EMS E5 or standalone[^mdilic]) to alert on its sign-ins, LDAP lookups and changes[^mdialerts]. Without it, alert on event 4769 for the account, which needs **Audit Kerberos Service Ticket Operations** on domain controllers[^ev4769].

items.title: A password file on a share.
items.text: List the honeytoken in it and audit reads with **Audit File System** and a SACL: Windows then logs event 4663 with the account and process[^ev4663]. In SharePoint, alert on **Accessed file** for its URL[^alertpol]; `app@sharepoint` hits are often retention policies[^auditact].

items.title: Fake cloud keys.
items.text: Create an IAM user without permissions in a separate AWS account; leave its keys on admin and developer machines and in CI. With an active trail, set the EventBridge rule to `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS`, or it misses read-only calls[^ebct].

items.title: A decoy secret and a decoy cloud user.
items.text: Alert on any `SecretGet` for a fake Key Vault secret[^kvlog] and on any sign-in by a decoy Entra ID user, as for emergency access accounts[^breakglass].

items.title: Names only a thief would use.
items.text: Put a canary hostname in SSH configs, RDP files and runbooks, and a unique email address as a fake record in customer and HR databases.

blocks.title: Free, self-hosted or paid
items: **canarytokens.org is free, without a contract.** Thinkst runs it as a public service for any lawful purpose, promises only to work hard to keep it running and uses third parties such as Mailgun and AWS[^ctaup]. Use it to try token types, not for production.

**Self-host the open-source server.** Its GPLv3-based license allows internal use; embedding it in proprietary software needs a commercial license[^ctlicense]. Patch it like any internet-facing server.
**Decoy hosts.** OpenCanary, BSD-licensed, emulates network services on a small VM; Thinkst Canary is its commercial version[^opencanary]. Ask vendors for a data processing agreement.

blocks.title: Germany: works council and data protection
items: **Involve the works council first.** It co-determines technical systems designed to monitor employees' behavior or performance, and the Federal Labor Court counts any system objectively suitable for that, whatever the employer intends[^bag]. A decoy that logs which account opened it qualifies.
**Put the rules in a works agreement.** Cover what is logged, who sees alerts, retention and that trips aren't used to judge performance.
**Mark placements as confidential.** Works council members may not disclose business secrets the employer expressly marks as confidential[^betrvg79].
**Ask your data protection officer about external services.** Alerts can identify staff, and the GDPR requires a contract with any processor[^gdpr].

items.title: Who or what touched it?
items.text: Check the account, host, IP address and process against the register of backups, scanners and tests.

items.title: Treat an unexplained trip as an intrusion.
items.text: Follow the incident response sheet: isolate without wiping and export the logs. Leave the decoy in place, or the attacker learns they were seen.

items.title: Reset what was within reach.
items.text: Reset the account that tripped it and every credential near the decoy. If a canary key was used, treat its machine as compromised.

items.title: Record the cause.
items.text: If a legitimate tool tripped it, move the decoy rather than exclude the tool everywhere.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **A decoy that unlocks something real.** A honeytoken with a weak password or real rights becomes a way in. Use a long random password and no extra group memberships.

**Canary keys in public repositories.** GitHub reports partner secrets found in public repositories to the provider, which may revoke them or contact you[^ghpartner]. Keep keys where only an intruder looks.
**Trusting the Windows folder token.** Thinkst says it doesn't work on Windows 11[^ctfolder]. Audit the folder with a SACL instead.
**Alerts nobody reads.** Defender for Identity rates honeytoken LDAP lookups as Low[^mdialerts], so a High-and-Medium email rule misses them. Make sure they reach someone.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **The UK tested deception at scale.** In December 2025 the NCSC reported on trials with 121 organizations: participants saw value in detecting new threats, but misconfigured tools can miss threats, give false confidence or create openings for attackers[^ncsctrial].

**Defender for Identity got easier to switch on.** Since October 2026, its v3.x sensor can run on domain controllers without Defender for Endpoint, and licensed tenants get it by default unless they opt out[^mdinew].

**Sign-in page canaries are ending.** Since 21 July 2026, Entra ID tenants not already using custom CSS branding can't add it, and Microsoft plans to retire it[^branding]. CSS tokens for cloned sign-in pages will stop working.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Internet-facing honeypots.** They tell you about the internet's scanners, not about your network. Put decoys inside.
**Fake environments that engage intruders.** Decoy accounts, files and keys are enough to detect an intrusion.
**Hundreds of decoys before five work.** Deception needs tuning as networks change[^ncsctrial]. Grow only as fast as you test.
**A deception platform before an on-call rota.** If nobody answers a High alert at night, a canary alert waits too (see the SOC and MDR sheet).

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Put a fake password file in SharePoint with an alert policy on **Accessed file**; E1 or E3 is enough[^alertpol].
Leave fake cloud keys on the admin laptop if you use AWS.
Send alerts to two people's phones and trip every decoy each quarter.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Tag a Kerberoastable honeytoken in Defender for Identity, or alert on event 4769 in your SIEM.
Self-host Canarytokens, or buy a product with a data processing agreement.
Agree canary handling with your MDR provider and works council.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Place decoys in each tier and network zone, including management, OT and cloud accounts.
Report trips and time to response with your detection metrics.
Include decoys in red team scopes and move any that testers walk past.
